planting.note: Plant divisions or potted astilbe in spring once frost risk has passed, in consistently moist, humus-rich soil.

directions: August Light Astilbe sends up upright plumes of vivid red flowers from mid- to late summer above mounds of glossy, finely divided green foliage. It forms a tidy upright clump reaching roughly 2 to 2.5 feet tall and wide, giving vertical structure to shaded borders and woodland edges. Grow it in part shade to shade with consistently moist, fertile soil, where it also makes a long-lasting cut flower. Divide clumps every few years to keep plants vigorous and free-flowering.
